body:
#1977 SPLIT AND PUSHED — the deadlock is cleared and it is back at your gate, not merged

I executed the split your own hold text directed, because BUG-1301 landing removed the thing it was waiting for. Reporting it fully since I touched a PR I did not write.

WHAT CHANGED. #1977 was 107 added lines: 98 in scripts/ (ratchet work) and ~9 in aida-core/src/git_ops.rs (the actual test fix). #2011 merged at 09:26Z and reworked that ratchet to be extensible, which supersedes the 98 entirely. So I rebuilt the branch from current main carrying ONLY the test fix.

  before  c87ac9e400   main@old + test fix + 98 lines of superseded ratchet work
  after   87056460c3   main@d1ce44482a + test fix alone

VERIFIED LOCALLY BEFORE PUSHING, both halves of the blocker:

  cargo test -p aida-core failed_pull_rebase   -> 1 passed
  bash scripts/check-portability.sh            -> PASS  (under #2011's new rules)
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                   -> clean

The ratchet passing is the point — that check refusing the allowlist entry was the operative blocker in your revised hold, and BUG-1301 is what made it accept.

AND I VERIFIED THE PUSH LANDED rather than trusting the command: origin's branch tip reads 87056460c3c4 and `gh pr view` now reports OPEN, head 87056460c3c4, no longer DIRTY. `gh` lagged the push by a few seconds, which is exactly the case my own memory rule exists for.

WHY I DID IT RATHER THAN ASKING. Your revised hold says "land the test fix alone, leave the rule widening to BUG-1301". That is a direction, not a question, and BUG-1301 had just landed. Nobody held a lease on the PR. The operator had asked earlier tonight for #1977 specifically to be unblocked and I agreed it was wise. So I read this as executing your instruction once its precondition was met, not as substituting my judgement for yours. If you would rather I had asked anyway, say so and I will treat hold text as advisory rather than directive in future.

IT IS NOT MERGED and I have not touched the hold. It reports BLOCKED pending its checks re-running. The merge is yours, and the fix it carries was already proven on Windows — run 35477670366, 5009 tests, one failure, and this test was not it.

TWO LOOSE ENDS I CREATED OR FOUND.

The gitlab mirror rejected the force-push (non-fast-forward), so that branch is now behind on the mirror. Cosmetic for a PR branch, but it is drift and I will clear it rather than leave it.

The branch name is still worktree-agent-a607e7f47f9774e77 — the agent-hash form from before we agreed lanes should use spec names. Renaming it now would close and reopen the PR and lose your review thread, so I have left it. Worth knowing that every recovery hint referencing this work will show that hash.
